summary: Persistent 429s after enabling client-side automatic retries with idempotency keys
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports sudden, sustained 429 responses after they enabled automatic client retries using idempotency keys in their upload pipeline. Impact: batch ingestion jobs that previously completed within quota are now failing consistently with 429s and producing inflated token/billing counts.

Impact:
- ~20% of nightly ingestion worker runs fail with 429s and get delayed by retry loops.
- Customer sees apparent quota exhaustion on a single API key despite overall tenant quota headroom.
- Billing shows duplicate token accounting spikes around the same windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool, prod/us-east
- SDK: lexi-upload-sdk v2.3.1 (client-side retry enabled by default)
- Edge path: customer -> partner edge proxy -> Redwood API GW -> rate limiter -> serving nodes

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Configure client with automatic retries (exponential backoff) + idempotency-key header per request.
2) Start 50 parallel worker threads uploading small batches (1–5 requests/sec each).
3) Kill the partner edge proxy for 10s to trigger transient 502s.
4) On recovery, many requests are retried by client and some fail with 429s shortly after.

Logs / Evidence:
- Customer provided request traces showing repeated POSTs with same idempotency-key but different edge-proxy source IPs and different request IDs.
- Billing spike CSV attached (tokens counted doubled for window 02:00–02:15 UTC).
- Support capture of sample X-Request-ID headers: [rwd-req-1432, rwd-req-1433, rwd-req-1435] showing rapid retries.

Initial hypothesis:
- Retries are reaching different edge nodes after a partner edge proxy failover, and upstream normalization drops idempotency header or rewrites path, causing the rate limiter to count retries as separate requests instead of de-duping by idempotency key.

Workaround suggested to customer:
- Temporarily disable automatic retries in lexi-upload-sdk.
- Throttle concurrency and add client-side jitter until we confirm root cause.

investigation_notes: Confirmed that partner edge failover creates multi-path fanout causing retries to land on different api-gateway instances.

Rate limiter dedupe flow uses an in-memory 'in-flight' marker then commits to centralized dedupe store on success; race observed when second attempt arrives while first is still in-flight -> double-count.
Deduce root cause: dedupe store commit is asynchronous and TTL for in-flight marker (500ms) too short relative to inter-node routing jitter, allowing quick retries to bypass dedupe.
Reproduced with stresstest harness: emulate 100ms jitter + 600ms commit delay -> ~17% duplicate accounting on retries.
Billing spikes correlate with windows where partner edge performed rolling restarts (confirmed via partner logs).
resolution:
Root cause: race in deduplication path within rate-limiter when idempotency-based de-dupe commit is delayed; quick client retries (enabled in lexi-upload-sdk) against multi-path edge lead to duplicate counting and 429s. Fix deployed in two parts: (1) rate-limiter change to use a short-lived centralized 'reserved' token that is set atomically on first receipt (https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/2043) and (2) backfill patch to extend in-flight marker TTL to 2s for dedicated pools. Rollout: Canary to us-east on 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC, full rollout 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.

Customer remediation: advised to re-enable retries only after full rollout and upgrade lexi-upload-sdk to v2.3.4 which adds optional "dedupe-safe" retry mode.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem and runbook update to document idempotency dedupe semantics across shards (owner: Dana Kim, due 2026-03-20).
- Add monitoring alert for duplicate token accounting >5% baseline in 15m window (owner: SRE team).
- Reach out to partner edge team to coordinate smoother handoff behaviour (action owner: Marco Ruiz).

Ticket status: In Progress (fix is deployed to canary; monitoring looks good).
